title: High-Performing Networking & Databases
oneLiner: Deliver content globally and pick the right database so reads and writes stay fast at scale.
examWeightNote: Completes Design High-Performing Architectures (24% of the exam).
objectives: Use CloudFront and Global Accelerator to reduce global latency.
Choose the right database: RDS/Aurora, DynamoDB, ElastiCache, Redshift, based on the access pattern.
Scale reads with RDS read replicas and Aurora, and scale throughput with DynamoDB.
Understand DynamoDB DAX and Aurora Global Database for performance/global reach.

services.name: Amazon CloudFront
services.purpose: CDN that caches content at edge locations for low-latency global delivery.

services.name: AWS Global Accelerator
services.purpose: Routes users over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint via anycast static IPs.

services.name: Amazon RDS / Aurora
services.purpose: Managed relational databases; Aurora adds high performance, storage auto-scaling, and up to 15 read replicas.

services.name: Amazon DynamoDB
services.purpose: Serverless key-value/document database with single-digit-millisecond latency at any scale.

services.name: Amazon Redshift
services.purpose: Managed petabyte-scale data warehouse for analytics/OLAP queries.

keyConcepts: CloudFront caches static and dynamic content at edge locations, cutting latency and offloading origins; pair it with S3 or ALB origins.
Global Accelerator improves performance for non-HTTP and TCP/UDP workloads by sending traffic over the AWS backbone to the closest healthy endpoint (great for gaming, VoIP, failover).
Use RDS read replicas (async) to scale read-heavy relational workloads; Aurora supports up to 15 low-lag replicas and an Aurora Global Database for cross-Region reads.
Choose DynamoDB for massive scale, predictable low-latency key-value access, and serverless operations; add DAX for microsecond cached reads.
Match the database to the pattern: relational/ACID → RDS/Aurora; key-value at scale → DynamoDB; analytics → Redshift; in-memory cache → ElastiCache.

scenarios.scenario: A read-heavy reporting dashboard hammers a single RDS MySQL instance, and read queries are slowing down the primary that also handles writes.
scenarios.question: What is the most appropriate way to scale the read load?

options.label: Add RDS read replicas and direct read traffic to them
Migrate the database to a single larger instance only

scenarios.explanation: Read replicas offload read traffic from the primary, scaling reads horizontally. Multi-AZ is for availability (its standby doesn't serve reads). Bigger storage/instances only scale vertically to a point.

scenarios.scenario: A global mobile game needs the lowest possible latency to a set of regional game servers, using TCP/UDP, with fast failover to healthy Regions and static entry-point IPs.
scenarios.question: Which service best meets this?

options.label: An internet-facing ALB in one Region

scenarios.explanation: Global Accelerator provides static anycast IPs and routes TCP/UDP traffic over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint with fast failover — ideal for latency-sensitive, non-HTTP workloads. CloudFront is optimized for cacheable HTTP content.

quiz.question: What is Amazon CloudFront primarily used for?
options: Caching and delivering content from edge locations to reduce latency
quiz.answer: Caching and delivering content from edge locations to reduce latency
quiz.explanation: CloudFront is AWS's CDN — it caches content at global edge locations close to users, lowering latency and offloading the origin.

quiz.question: Which database is the best fit for a serverless application needing single-digit-millisecond key-value reads at massive scale?
quiz.explanation: DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL key-value/document store delivering consistent low-latency performance at any scale — ideal for high-throughput key-value access.

quiz.question: How do RDS read replicas help performance?
options: They provide synchronous failover for availability
They offload read queries from the primary, scaling reads horizontally
quiz.answer: They offload read queries from the primary, scaling reads horizontally
quiz.explanation: Read replicas asynchronously copy data and serve read traffic, relieving the primary. (Multi-AZ standbys, by contrast, are for availability, not read scaling.)

quiz.question: Which service accelerates DynamoDB reads to microsecond latency via an in-memory cache?
quiz.explanation: DAX is a fully managed in-memory cache for DynamoDB that reduces read latency from milliseconds to microseconds for read-heavy workloads.
